# Client

`AwsSecretsManagerClient` is the entry point. Create one per process (or per set of credentials), share
it between threads/tasks and close it on shutdown. Service functions hang off the client (see
[Functions](functions.md)).

<!-- @sdk-kit:keep functions — service-owned: client functions and their AWS Secrets Manager behaviour; kept by "sdk-kit sync" -->

| Function | Returns | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| constructor / `create` / `new` / `builder()` | client | validates the config (`CONFIG` error); region, credentials, endpoint override (`url`), assume role, timeouts, retries, proxy and TLS go to the AWS SDK client |
| `fromEnv()` | client | config from `GROW_AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_*` > standard `AWS_*` variables > AWS SDK default chain |
| `withSdkClient(client)` | client | wraps an existing AWS SDK client; `close()` leaves it open |
| `health()` | `HealthStatus { healthy, status, details }` | signed `ListSecrets {MaxResults: 1}`, no retries; **never throws** for an unhealthy or unreachable service (rejected credentials still count as reachable, `details.auth = "failed"`), only for `CANCELLED` and `CONFIG` |
| `ping()` | latency | the same call with retries; `AUTHENTICATION` on bad credentials, `PERMISSION_DENIED` without `secretsmanager:ListSecrets` |
| `serverVersion()` | — | always `UNSUPPORTED`: AWS exposes no server version (the API contract is the constant `API_VERSION`, `2017-10-17`) |
| `close()` | — | idempotent; stops the watchers of every provider from `secrets()` and releases the SDK client this instance built |

`status` is `ok`, `degraded` (throttled), `unhealthy` (HTTP 5xx) or `unreachable` (network error
or timeout). AWS-specific details are on [Client setup](functions/client-setup.md).

<!-- @sdk-kit:endkeep -->

## Create, use and close

<!-- @sdk-kit:keep examples — service-owned: create/use/close examples per language; kept by "sdk-kit sync" -->

=== "TypeScript"

    ```ts
    import { AwsSecretsManagerClient } from "@grow-codes/aws-secrets-manager";

    const client = new AwsSecretsManagerClient({ region: "eu-central-1" }); // or AwsSecretsManagerClient.fromEnv()
    try {
      const health = await client.health();          // { healthy, status, details }
      const latencyMs = await client.ping();         // number (ms)
      const secret = await client.getSecretValue("prod/app/db");

      // Cancellation and per-call deadline: every I/O method accepts { signal }
      const status = await client.health({ signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2_000) });
    } finally {
      await client.close();                          // safe to call twice
    }
    ```

=== "Rust"

    ```rust
    use grow_aws_secrets_manager::{AwsSecretsManagerClient, AwsSecretsManagerConfig};

    let config = AwsSecretsManagerConfig::builder().region("eu-central-1").build()?;
    let client = AwsSecretsManagerClient::new(config)?;
    let health = client.health().await?;          // HealthStatus
    let latency = client.ping().await?;           // Duration
    let secret = client.get_secret_value("prod/app/db", Default::default()).await?;
    client.close().await;                         // safe to call twice

    // Cancellation: drop the future, e.g. with a deadline
    let status = tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(2), client.health()).await;
    ```

    Without an async runtime, enable the `blocking` feature:

    ```rust
    let client = grow_aws_secrets_manager::blocking::AwsSecretsManagerClient::from_env()?;
    let health = client.health()?;
    ```

=== "Go"

    ```go
    client, err := asm.NewClient(asm.Config{Region: "eu-central-1"}) // or asm.NewClientFromEnv()
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    defer client.Close() // safe to call twice

    health, err := client.Health(ctx)                         // HealthStatus
    latency, err := client.Ping(ctx)                          // time.Duration
    secret, err := client.GetSecretValue(ctx, "prod/app/db", nil)

    // Cancellation and deadlines come from ctx
    ctx2, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    health, err = client.Health(ctx2)
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from grow_aws_secrets_manager import AwsSecretsManagerClient, AwsSecretsManagerConfig, CancelToken

    with AwsSecretsManagerClient(AwsSecretsManagerConfig(region="eu-central-1")) as client:
        health = client.health()           # HealthStatus
        latency_ms = client.ping()         # float (ms)
        secret = client.get_secret_value("prod/app/db")

        # Cancel from another thread
        token = CancelToken()
        health = client.health(cancel=token)
    # close() ran; calling it again is safe
    ```

    `AsyncAwsSecretsManagerClient` (aioboto3, extra `[async]`) has the same methods as coroutines
    (`await client.health()`, `await client.aclose()`, `async with`), and honours task cancellation.

=== "Java"

    ```java
    try (AwsSecretsManagerClient client =
        AwsSecretsManagerClient.builder().region("eu-central-1").build()) {
      HealthStatus health = client.health();
      Duration latency = client.ping();
      AwsSecretValue secret = client.getSecretValue("prod/app/db");

      // Async variants return CompletableFuture; cancel(true) cancels the request
      CompletableFuture<HealthStatus> pending = client.healthAsync();
      pending.orTimeout(2, TimeUnit.SECONDS).join();
    } // close() is idempotent
    ```

    For an emulator (Moto, LocalStack) set `url` (`GROW_AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_URL`), for example
    `http://127.0.0.1:5000`, together with a region and static credentials.

<!-- @sdk-kit:endkeep -->

## Lifecycle rules

- The client is safe for concurrent use. Reuse it: it keeps a connection pool.
- `close()` flushes queued work (for example log batches) within the configured deadline and is
  safe to call more than once. Any call on a closed client fails with `CANCELLED`
  (`"<operation>: client is closed"`).
- Each language also offers its idiomatic scope: TypeScript `try/finally`, Rust `close().await`
  (plus best-effort `Drop`), Go `defer client.Close()`, Python `with`/`async with`, Java
  try-with-resources.
